name: pcsc-lite
desc: Middleware to access a smart card using SCard API
why: Middleware for smart card readers, a door into APDU and smartcard protocols most developers never touch.

brief.what_it_is: pcsc-lite is a middleware library and daemon that gives applications access to smart card readers through the PC/SC API (SCard API). Client programs call the standard SCard functions, and the pcscd daemon talks to the physical reader and its driver, typically via USB. Its executables include pcscd, the daemon, and pcsc-spy, a debugging tool that spies on API calls. The project site describes it as 'Middleware to access a smart card using SCard API (PC/SC).' Input is smart card reader hardware with cards inserted, and output is card responses to APDU commands, returned to the calling application.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames it as a free, portable implementation of the PC/SC standard for smart card access. The project was started by David Corcoran in 1999, and Ludovic Rousseau has been the main author since 2001.
brief.how_it_works: The site does not describe the internal architecture in detail. It mentions a card movement notification mechanism, card auto power on and off, and pcscd auto start through systemd. Its debug section describes an API spy built on the LIBPCSCLITE_DELEGATE mechanism. The homepage also notes that PC/SC clients and the server can run on two different hosts.

Support-log recipe: kill any running pcscd, then run it in the foreground with debug, APDU and color output, with the CCID driver log level set high, and save the output to log.txt for bug reports. The site warns that the PIN may appear in the log.
Support info: the site asks bug reporters to include the output of this command.

brief.install_notes: The site's build instructions use meson, with the commands listed above. Dependencies to install first: flex, meson, and libudev or libusb. libsystemd and polkit are optional. Packages are also available as pcscd, libpcsclite1 and libpcsclite-dev, plus packages in many other distributions. The site says you should not need to build it on macOS, because Apple reimplemented PC/SC on top of CryptoTokenKit. Source downloads and the git repository are on Debian salsa and GitHub.
brief.standout: It is the reference open-source PC/SC implementation on Linux and the base for much smart card tooling. The site includes a built-in API spy (pcsc-spy) and a documented debug mode that logs APDU traffic in full. That gives an unusual view into smartcard conversations, which most developers never see.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but the evidence is thin. The GitHub README (LudovicRousseau/PCSC) is a short stub that links to the project site. The site's license text covers copyright through 2024, and it documents a meson build. I did not find a release date or last-commit date in the pages I could read, so I cannot confirm the release cadence.
brief.caveats: The GitHub repository at LudovicRousseau/pcsc-lite returned 404. The working repository is LudovicRousseau/PCSC. Support is by mailing list (pcsclite-muscle), not a bug tracker in the pages I read. The site says it is not tested by the author on the BSDs, and that HP-UX may have worked long ago. Solaris ships its own fork. The main code is under a BSD-like license, but some source files use other licenses, so the COPYING file must be checked. The debug log can include the PIN.

entry.title: pcsc-lite
entry.tldr: The open-source PC/SC daemon for smart card readers, with a spy mode that logs the raw APDU conversations between software and a card.
entry.deeper_look:
pcsc-lite is middleware that lets programs talk to smart card readers through the standard PC/SC API (the SCard functions). Applications call the API, and the pcscd daemon talks to the reader and its driver, usually over USB. What comes back are the card's responses to APDU commands, the small request and reply packets smart cards speak.

The project was started by David Corcoran in 1999, and Ludovic Rousseau has been the main author since 2001. The homepage presents it as a free, portable implementation of the PC/SC standard. Much Linux smart card tooling sits on top of it, so it is the layer between a card and whatever reads it.

The interesting part is the debugging. pcscd can run in the foreground with debug and APDU logging turned on, and pcsc-spy can watch the API calls an application makes. Together they show the conversation between software and a card, which most developers never see. The homepage also mentions that PC/SC clients and the server can run on two different hosts.
entry.install:
brew install pcsc-lite
Needs a USB smart card reader and a card to see anything real. On macOS the site says you should not need it, because Apple reimplemented PC/SC on top of CryptoTokenKit.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the daemon's options, including the foreground and debug flags.
Runs the daemon in the foreground and prints every APDU exchange in color, saving it to log.txt. The site warns the log can contain your PIN.
Shows how to use the API spy that records the SCard calls an application makes.

entry.whats_unique: It is the reference open-source PC/SC implementation on Linux, and it ships with a documented APDU logging mode and an API spy, so you can watch a smart card conversation directly.
entry.caveats: You need a reader and a card for anything interesting to happen, the author does not test on the BSDs, and debug logs can leak your PIN.
